name: Desktop
description: Desktop conveniences: clipboard, audio, volume, media, notifications, and opening, listing and closing apps.
author: PAI

capabilities.confirmationReason: Reading clipboard contents can be sensitive. Please confirm that you want to read the clipboard.
Writing to the clipboard can be sensitive. Please confirm that you want to write to the clipboard.

capabilities.description: Play an audio file or URL in the background.
Speak text via the system TTS engine.

capabilities.confirmationReason: Reading desktop notifications can be sensitive. Please confirm that you want to read the notifications.
capabilities.description: List recent desktop notifications. Requires the dunst notification daemon; other desktops return 'not_supported'.

capabilities.confirmationReason: Dismissing desktop notifications can be sensitive. Please confirm that you want to dismiss the notifications.
capabilities.description: Dismiss all desktop notifications. Requires the dunst notification daemon; other desktops return an error.
Get, set, mute or unmute the default audio output volume.

level.description: Volume percent; required when action is 'set'.

capabilities.description: Launch a desktop app or open a file/URL. To open a local file use url with file:// scheme (e.g. 'file:///home/user/image.jpg'). To launch an app by name use the app field. Fire-and-forget: an app started this way can NOT be closed later. Use app.open if the user may ask to close it.
capabilities.confirmationReason: Launching applications or opening URLs can be sensitive. Please confirm that you want to proceed.

app.description: Application name to launch (e.g., 'firefox', 'eog', 'spotify'). Do NOT include file arguments here — use the url field for files.

url.description: URL or local file to open with the default handler. For local files use file:// scheme, e.g. 'file:///home/chethan/Pictures/image.jpg'. For web URLs use https://.

capabilities.confirmationReason: Opening an application, file or link can be sensitive. Please confirm that you want to proceed.
capabilities.description: Open an app, a local file (url with file:// or an absolute path) or a web link, in a way PAI keeps track of so it can be closed later with app.close. Pass app (name or id, e.g. 'calculator'), url, or both (open that file in that app). Returns a handle. If the app was already running and just took the request, closable is false and it cannot be closed by PAI.

app.description: Application name or desktop id, e.g. 'calculator' or 'org.gnome.Calculator'.

url.description: File (file:// URL or absolute path) or web link to open. With no app, the default application is used.

capabilities.confirmationReason: Closing an application can lose unsaved work. Please confirm that you want to close it.
capabilities.description: Close an app that PAI opened with app.open. Identify it by handle (from app.open / app.list) or by app name; with neither, closes the only open app. Only apps opened with app.open can be closed, never other apps or ones started with app.launch. Graceful first; force=true kills an app that will not exit.

app.description: Name of an app PAI opened, e.g. 'calculator'.

force.description: Kill the app if it does not exit gracefully.

capabilities.description: List the apps PAI has open (handle, app name, what it was opened with) and can close with app.close.

changelog.summary: Apps can now be opened in a way PAI can close again: new app.open, app.close and app.list.
features: app.open: open an app, file or link as an app PAI tracks, returns a handle
app.close: close an app that app.open started (graceful, with an optional force)
app.list: list the apps PAI has open
fixes: app.launch results now say closable=false (use app.open when the app may need closing)
